header: Questions that fold open one at a time
lead: Two to thirty rows, all closed on first paint so the page stays scannable. Everything below is native browser behaviour — this element ships no script of any kind.

questions.title: How is the exclusive behaviour done without a script?
questions.bodytext: Every row is a details element and they all share one name attribute. The browser then treats them as a group and closes the open row when another is opened — the same relationship a set of radio buttons has.

questions.title: What happens to find-in-page?
questions.bodytext: It still works. Browsers open a closed disclosure to reveal a match, which a scripted accordion built from divs and hidden attributes has to reimplement, usually badly.

questions.title: Do the questions appear in the page outline?
questions.bodytext: Yes. Each summary contains a level-three heading, so a reader navigating by heading can move between the questions without opening any of them.

questions.title: Can two accordions sit on one page?
questions.bodytext: They can. The shared name is keyed to the record, so each block forms its own exclusive group and neither closes the other's rows.
